answer: Basalt Kernel Audit: 1) A participant locks a basalt token bond to become an evaluator. 2) The central software kernel assigns evaluations across the system bridge. 3) The bridge network randomly spot-checks 5 percent of tasks; corrupt entries forfeit their full $200 bond. Creating N fake identities requires an explicit capital lock of $200 x N, meaning twenty sybils freeze $4000. This protocol collapses if the inspection rate drops to zero, letting unvetted nodes retain their deposits while submitting garbage. The automated trap acts like a tripwire triggering a deadfall.
